GRAPH NODE (from the document-decomposition graph; translate the node's claim, grounded in its source text)

ESTABLISHES (the one claim this module must express):
The voice_style section contains style guidelines specifically for audio and video conversations, and there are two separate systems for audio communication: Standard voice mode and Advanced voice mode.

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  - standard_voice_mode: Standard voice mode, where automatic speech recognition transcribes the user's voice into text and the assistant's textual responses are converted to speech via a separate text-to-speech system.
  - advanced_voice_mode: Advanced voice mode, where the assistant natively receives audio input and produces audio output, and the user may choose to share video with the assistant.

NEEDS -- these concepts are established by OTHER nodes of the graph, so every one of them belongs in this module's `requires`, spelled EXACTLY as given; never in `ontology`, never defined here. `inputs` is only for plain facts about the situation being judged (messages, roles, case data) that YOU identify -- a name can never appear in both requires and inputs:
  - voice_style_guidelines: The style guidelines in the voice_style section apply to both standard and advanced voice modes; instructions about audio/video nuances apply only to advanced voice.

CITATION: every ontology/asserts entry that cites a source must cite EXACTLY 'l4252_4482_n001' -- the id of this node. Never cite line numbers, line ranges, or any other id.

SOURCE TEXT (verbatim from the document; the L-numbers locate text, they are not citable ids):
